title: review: S3c memory feeds skills and strategy: recurring procedural memory becomes learned-skill candidates, promoted skills are referenced from memory, workflow strategy outcomes live as structured WARM records with a Planner query (P30, P31)
spec:
orchestrator/skill_learning.py: add candidates_from_memory(root) using memory_store.search over kinds gotcha and decision: group records by shared components (at least 3 records over at least 2 distinct dates) whose bodies contain procedural language (imperative verbs such as run, check, set, use, never, always, before, after) and produce learned-skill proposals through the existing proposal path (same shape and quarantine/testing lifecycle as today's learned skills; provenance memory with the record ids). When a proposal's skill is promoted to active, memory_store.add records a tag skill:<skill_id> on each source record and memory_hot renders such records as one line pointing at the skill instead of the full body. orchestrator/strategy.py: at merge time (new hook: daemon.py joins the scope; in the merge path that marks a task merged, call strategy.record_outcome(task, state_dir=STATE) (daemon.py already binds the name root to failures.root; never shadow it) which computes the token, usd, duration and fix-round figures the way strategy.observations() does today and writes the record) write one memory_store record kind strategy per merged execute task: title '<task_class> <band> <strategy name>', tags task_class:<x>, band:<b>, strategy:<name>, outcome first_pass|fix_rounds:<n>, body with tokens, duration, executor, fix rounds; source_task and source_goal set. CLI `orchestrator memory strategies [--task-class x] [--band b] [--json]` aggregates strategy records: per strategy name the count, first-pass rate, median tokens and duration, so the Planner asks what worked for this kind of task without reading retrospectives. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/17-memory-skills-strategy.md.
Spec review T-1182 folded in: (1) The merge-time hook is new (daemon.py never called strategy.py): implement strategy.record_outcome(task, root) reusing the computation of strategy.observations(), called from the daemon's merge path (scope adds orchestrator/daemon.py and tests/test_daemon.py). (2) Tagging source records with skill:<skill_id> lives inside skills_registry.transition() when the new state is active (scope adds orchestrator/skills_registry.py), so both `skills promote` and the generic `skills transition` paths tag. (3) Proposals from memory get roles = the union of the role fields of the source records' source tasks (looked up on the bus when present) with 'execute' as the default, never an empty list; a test asserts a proposal is selectable for execute. (4) Record shape for strategy records: Record.outcome holds first_pass or fix_rounds:<n>; tags carry only task_class:<x>, band:<b>, strategy:<name>; `memory strategies` aggregates on those fields.
Spec review T-1192 folded in: (1) root conventions are explicit: memory_store and memory_hot take the REPO root (Path(root)/'.orchestrator'/...), strategy, skill_learning and skills_registry take the .orchestrator STATE directory; when one calls the other, convert (state_dir.parent for the repo root) and say so in a comment; the tests follow each module's harness convention. (2) The merge hook resolves the lineage root first (attribution.lineage / strategy._root_id) so a fix-round merge records the outcome for the root task; one record per merged lineage root. (3) Strategy record id is deterministic and unique per task: id = 'strategy-<task_id>' passed explicitly to memory_store.add, never derived from kind/date/title. (4) Roles for memory-sourced proposals: read the source tasks' JSON from state_dir/tasks/<id>.json the way skill_learning._tasks does, never bus.get; missing files count as no role; default ['execute']. (5) Confidence for memory-sourced patterns: min(1.0, records/5) multiplied by min(1.0, distinct_dates/3), evidence_strength = record count; the existing propose() threshold (0.6) applies unchanged, so a group needs at least 3 records over at least 2 dates and typically 3 dates to pass; document the formula in 17-memory-skills-strategy.md.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Task worktrees carry no .orchestrator runs, tasks or decision_log state: tests use synthetic fixtures; for any measured numbers in docs run read-only against /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/.orchestrator via an explicit root argument. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Contracts of the earlier modules: .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and docs/hermes-hardening/*.md on this branch; read the merged modules before building on them.
acceptance: tests/test_strategy.py::test_record_outcome_uses_lineage_root_and_unique_id (a fix-round merge writes one strategy-<root id> record; two same-day tasks keep separate records)

result.summary: All scoped acceptance items are implemented. Root conventions are handled with comments. The strategy record id is deterministic (strategy-<root id>). The lineage root is resolved. The confidence formula and roles defaults match the spec. Only the unguarded merge-path hook is worth changing before merge.

comments.issue: strategy.record_outcome runs unguarded in report_merge after the merge has succeeded. A memory_store or sqlite error, or a missing task file, would raise out of the merge path and skip whatever follows, even though the merge is already done. Wrap it in try/except and log, since the record is telemetry only.

candidates_from_memory does not skip records that already carry a skill:<id> tag. After a skill is promoted, the same records keep re-qualifying and get re-proposed on every `skills learn`. Filter out tagged records.

Memory record bodies are copied verbatim into the evidence and the proposal. They are untrusted DB rows. The quarantine lifecycle contains this, but confirm that the context scanner inspects memory-sourced proposals before they reach testing.
The record date uses date.today(), not the merge time or the task's timestamp. It is only correct if record_outcome runs at merge. A replay or backfill would date the record wrongly.
